title: Chapter 18: Azure Dragon Carp
paragraphs: "My teacher is a Pill Refiner, but I haven't earned my certification yet due to my age," the white-robed girl said. "I'd like to remind readers to remember our domain: sto55.com."
Not every cultivator can apply for certification in the Hundred Arts of Cultivation. The Immortal Sect sets age and specialization requirements to streamline the process and reduce annual workload.
For example, high school students like Chen Mobai wouldn't meet the minimum age requirement.
The white-robed girl was in the same situation.
The sole drawback of Water Method Pill Refining is its time-consuming nature. It's nearly impossible for a single Pill Refiner to oversee the entire process from start to finish.
While Immortal Sect regulations stipulate that only certified Pill Refiners can concoct medicinal formulas, apprentices and assistants are tacitly allowed to handle simpler auxiliary ingredients.
Chen Mobai surmised that the white-robed girl was likely an Apothecary in training.

He recalled the Spirit Water refinement methods described in theBlackwater Art. Still lacking clarity on the matter, he considered asking for guidance but hesitated to speak without a proper introduction.
"Farewell," Chen Mobai finally said, turning to leave the pharmacy.
"Such a strange person," Qing Nü murmured. She sensed he had wanted to ask something but couldn't understand why he'd ultimately held back.
Watching the young man's retreating figure disappear around the street corner, she shook her head and returned to the back room to continue extracting medicinal herbs.
Water Abode.
Chen Mobai nervously pulled out the black Array Flag. The massive hemispherical barrier above his head began to ripple slightly.

Immediately, he followed the Spiritual Power channeling technique described in Chan Si's training materials, injecting Spiritual Power into the Array Flag. With his other hand, he performed two simple hand seals.
Moments later, a perfectly circular, flawless opening two meters in diameter appeared in the barrier, following the direction indicated by the Black Flag.
Suppressing his excitement, Chen Mobai reinserted the Array Flag and approached the entrance he had created in the barrier.
With a slightly trembling hand, he reached out of the barrier, his fingertips brushing against the water outside.
Cool and refreshing, the water felt as smooth as silk.
After playing with the water for a while and confirming there were no immediate dangers, Chen Mobai cautiously extended half his body through the opening.
Having not cultivated any water-repelling spells, he had to rely on holding his breath. Even with this limitation, he managed to glimpse the scenery beyond the Water Abode.
It was a lake of immeasurable size, its horizon stretching beyond his vision. The lakebed was carpeted with blue-glowing aquatic plants, their luminescent glow stark against the dim environment.
Among the aquatic plants, schools of azure carp darted back and forth, playfully weaving through the greenery.
Chen Mobai confirmed that these were the same fish he had eaten earlier.
Raising his Needle Case, he channeled the Five Elements Art, infusing it with spiritual power. A golden ray of light shot forth.

Though still a bit clumsy with this magic tool, Chen Mobai, sparing no spiritual power, launched the Flying Needle in a straight line. With no need for finesse, the needle pierced through the azure carp before it could escape.

Seeing his successful catch, Chen Mobai raised his other hand. Two glass beads, imbued with his Five Elements Art's spiritual power, flew out like twin iridescent rainbows, clasping the slowly sinking carcass of the carp.
After retrieving both his meal and the Flying Needle, Chen Mobai replanted the Black Flag, resealing the Azure Water Formation's opening.

He first carefully examined the azure carp in his hand. A deep indigo line ran along its dorsal ridge like a sinew, and two long whiskers protruded from its mouth. The fish felt icy-cold to the touch, like holding a block of ice.
"How does this carp resemble the Azure Dragon Carp, a second-tier Protected Spiritual Beast of the Immortal Sect?"

Chen Mobai murmured to himself, "The Azure Dragon Carp's bloodline traces back to an Azure Flood Dragon deep in the sea, a creature the Immortal Sect barely managed to capture when they first explored the ocean realms."

Legend had it that when prepared in a special manner and consumed by cultivators, the Azure Dragon Carp's flesh would release a trace of the Azure Flood Dragon's essence, randomly increasing the consumer's Water Spiritual Root attribute points by 1 to 5.

However, the Immortal Sect's Azure Dragon Carp are only cultivated at the Kunpeng Dao Academy, where they are regarded as the exclusive preserve of the Nascent Soul Venerables. Twenty years ago, this venerable even added wild Azure Dragon Carp to the Immortal Sect's latest Protected Spiritual Beast list, completely forbidding cultivators from killing them for food.
Chen Mobai hesitated for a moment, but ultimately couldn't resist the temptation. He retrieved the dagger he had obtained from the old man.
Immortal Sect regulations stated that while wild Azure Dragon Carp were protected, cultivated ones could be eaten.
Though these azure carp bore some resemblance to Azure Dragon Carp, distinct differences remained. They lacked spiritual energy and were raised outside the Water Abode, thus qualifying as cultivated.
With practiced precision, Chen Mobai scaled, gutted, filleted, and sliced the fish in a single, fluid motion.
This dagger wasn't a Magic Tool, but it was incredibly sharp. He'd once sliced through gold as easily as tofu, making it overkill for filleting fish.
This time, he planned to eat it chilled, bringing ice cubes and seasonings from home.
However, the fish itself was already icy cold, so he could skip the chilling process.
Chen Mobai even grabbed a can of carbonated drink. If he'd had a stemmed glass, the whole setup would have felt even more ceremonial.
Too bad he was eating alone.

A faint sense of regret accompanied the first bite of the cold, tender fish. Paired with the aged black vinegar he'd ordered online from Wangwu Grotto-Heaven, an indescribable burst of sour, tingling, and refreshing flavors erupted on his taste buds.

As the fish entered his stomach, a cool energy surged through his body, making him shiver before settling into a profound sense of comfort and invigoration, like taking a cold shower on a sweltering summer day—utterly blissful and refreshing.
After finishing, Chen Mobai let out a satisfied burp. His first thought was:Cooking that first fish was such a waste!
Of course, he hadn't forgotten his primary task.
After cleaning up with a Cleansing Spell, he sat cross-legged on his Meditation Cushion and circulated the Five Elements Art through a complete cycle.
Before the newly cultivated adaptive spiritual power could even return to his dantian, Chen Mobai intercepted a portion and channeled it into the newly purchased Spiritual Power Test Strip.
This simple tool was used to measure one's Spiritual Root, but it was only compatible with cultivators of the Five Elements Art.

In the Immortal Sect, everyone was a cultivator. Virtually every child began learning Qi Refining and immortal cultivation techniques during their formative years. To streamline the process of measuring Spiritual Roots, the Grand Medical Palace invented these Spiritual Power Test Strips.

As Chen Mobai's spiritual power was absorbed by the strip, it instantly stained the paper with five vibrant colors. Then, numerical values corresponding to the proportion of each Five Elements aura materialized on the surface:
Metal: 23, Wood: 27, Water: 25, Fire: 17, Earth: 10.
Sure enough, his Water Spiritual Root had increased by 2 points.
With this confirmation, Chen Mobai knew it was time for more experiments.
Forcing down his burning excitement, he rose again and reactivated the Azure Water Formation.
Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!
Golden streams of light erupted outside the Water Abode. One after another, the azure carp peacefully grazing on aquatic plants inexplicably became Chen Mobai's next meal.
